papers.title: Synthesis of Sb(iii)-immobilized on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes for efficient and green preparation of pyrazolopyranopyrimidines: comprehensive characterization, green chemistry evaluation and computational antifungal profiling against 5TZ1.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel heterogeneous nanocatalyst, Sb(iii) immobilized on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes (N-MSNTs/Sb(iii)), was successfully synthesized. This catalyst was then applied in a one-pot, four-component synthesis of pyrazolopyranopyrimidine derivatives via the condensation of ethyl acetoacetate, hydrazine hydrate, aromatic aldehydes, and barbituric/thiobarbituric acid. Comprehensive characterization using FT-IR, FE-SEM, EDS, HR-TEM, XRD, and BET/BJH analyses confirmed its structural features. Notably, HR-TEM revealed hollow nanotubular structures with an inner diameter o
papers.summary: This paper reports a new heterogeneous nanocatalyst made by immobilizing antimony on nitrogen-doped mesoporous silica nanotubes, which efficiently catalyzes a one-pot four-component reaction to make pyrazolopyranopyrimidine derivatives under green conditions. The catalyst is thoroughly characterized and the products are computationally profiled as potential antifungals against the 5TZ1 target. The work combines synthetic methodology with green chemistry metrics and docking-based bioactivity prediction.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational evaluation of atractylenolide III from Tubipora musica for anticancer lead identification.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health challenge, with over 900,000 new cases annually and a pronounced male predominance. In pursuit of novel, low-toxicity therapeutics, this study isolated Atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and demonstrated measurable, dose-dependent cytotoxic activity against HepG2 liver cancer cells, achieving an IC50 value of 15.50 µg/mL and reducing cell viability to 25.0% at 25 µg/mL. To investigate potential molecular targets and propose hypothetical mechanism pathways, we employed a multi-layered computational strategy. Mol
papers.summary: This study isolated atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and showed it kills HepG2 liver cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner (IC50 = 15.50 µg/mL). Computational docking and network analyses were then used to propose hypothetical molecular targets and mechanisms underlying the anticancer activity.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota and Aldosterone Regulate Natriuretic Peptide B Expression to Drive Mitophagy and Metabolic Reprogramming in Sepsis-Like Model of Myocardial Injury.
papers.abstract: Myocardial injury is a major contributor to mortality in sepsis, yet the mechanisms underlying gut-heart communication in sepsis-induced myocardial injury remain insufficiently defined. Natriuretic peptide B (NPPB) is a cardiac stress-responsive gene, but its involvement in mitochondrial homeostasis and metabolic regulation is unclear. This study investigated how gut microbiota and aldosterone influence myocardial mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming through NPPB in sepsis-induced myocardial injury.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbiota and aldosterone regulate the cardiac stress gene NPPB (natriuretic peptide B) to influence mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming in a sepsis-like model of myocardial injury. The findings suggest a gut-heart communication axis in which microbial and hormonal signals converge on NPPB to drive mitochondrial quality control and metabolic shifts in the injured heart.

papers.title: Kinetic, computational, and phylogenetic characterization of PA2125 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1: A hydroxybenzaldehyde dehydrogenase of the newly defined ALDH33 family.
papers.abstract: PA2125 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 is annotated as an aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), but its substrate specificity, catalytic properties, and phylogenetic family assignment had not been established. Here, we cloned the PA2125 gene, produced and purified the recombinant PA2125 protein, and combined extensive substrate screening and steady-state kinetic characterisation with molecular dockings, molecular dynamics simulations, and phylogenetic analysis. PA2125 preferred NAD⁺ over NADP⁺, and screening of 54 aldehydes revealed a narrow substrate range centred on substituted benzaldehydes, part
papers.summary: This study characterizes PA2125, a previously uncharacterized aldehyde dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1, showing it prefers NAD+ and acts specifically on substituted benzaldehydes. Combining enzyme kinetics, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and phylogenetics, the authors assign PA2125 to a newly defined ALDH33 family. The work establishes the substrate specificity and evolutionary placement of this enzyme, filling a gap in ALDH classification.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two method classes have distinct determinants of success, with performance diverging notably between the easier redocking and more realistic cross-docking scenarios.

papers.title: Reversible homodimerization of a small leucine-rich proteoglycan PRELP modulates the interactions with TGFβ1 and IGFI-R.
papers.abstract: Small leucine-rich proteoglycans (SLRPs) are responsible for various biological functions via their multiple interactions with various proteins. Although some SLRPs form homodimers, it remains unclear how homodimerization affects the molecular functions of SLRPs. Herein, we report the molecular basis and functional significance of homodimerization of PRELP, which is a member of SLRP family. We used biophysical techniques to validate the premise that PRELP forms a reversible homodimer in a concentration-dependent manner. Because the spatial aggregation propensity (SAP) calculation indicated tha
papers.summary: This study shows that the small leucine-rich proteoglycan PRELP reversibly forms homodimers in a concentration-dependent manner, and that this dimerization modulates its interactions with TGFβ1 and IGF1-R. The authors use biophysical methods and spatial aggregation propensity calculations to define the molecular basis of dimerization, suggesting a regulatory mechanism for SLRP function.

papers.title: Structure-based design of soluble prefusion-stabilized herpes simplex virus type 2 glycoprotein B antigens.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection causes recurrent genital herpes throughout life, yet no vaccines have been approved. Glycoprotein B (gB) is a class III fusion protein that mediates HSV-2 entry by transitioning from a metastable prefusion conformation to a stable postfusion conformation. Here, using structure-based design, we stabilize HSV-2 gB in its prefusion conformation. A 2.8 Å resolution cryo-EM structure reveals a closed state of prefusion gB, which differs from recently published open states. Vaccination of mice with protein subunit and mRNA-based vaccines of pre- and post
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based design to engineer HSV-2 glycoprotein B (gB) into a stable prefusion conformation, solving a 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure that reveals a closed prefusion state distinct from previously reported open states. The stabilized antigens were tested as protein subunit and mRNA vaccines in mice, providing a foundation for improved HSV-2 vaccine candidates.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Azobenzenoid Derivatives Against Trypanosomatid: RNA Editing Ligase 1 as a Potential Molecular Target.
papers.abstract: Neglected tropical diseases caused by pathogenic protozoa, including Chagas Disease (etiological agent Trypanosoma cruzi) and leishmaniasis (etiological agent Leishmania spp.), are public health problems in many developing countries.
papers.summary: This study combines experimental and computational approaches to investigate azobenzenoid derivatives as potential inhibitors of RNA editing ligase 1 (REL1) in trypanosomatid parasites that cause Chagas disease and leishmaniasis. The work identifies REL1 as a promising molecular target and evaluates the binding and activity of these compounds, aiming to advance drug development for neglected tropical diseases.

papers.title: Enhancing prediction accuracy for enzyme activity engineering through sequence co-evolution and epistatic relationship modeling.
papers.abstract: Conventional enzyme engineering strategies, such as directed evolution with structure-based analysis, are limited by laborious workflows and by the need to screen extensive enzyme libraries. Computational models based on multiple sequence alignment, such as SCANEER, have streamlined these engineering strategies, enabling the successful prediction of single-site mutations that enhance enzyme activity. However, when combining predicted mutations to improve enzyme performance or expand mutational space, such approaches often fail due to epistatic interactions among amino acid residues, which can
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method that improves prediction of enzyme-activity-enhancing mutations by incorporating sequence co-evolution and epistatic interactions between residues. It addresses the common failure of existing MSA-based tools like SCANEER when combining individually beneficial single mutations, which often break down due to epistasis. The approach aims to make computational enzyme engineering more reliable without exhaustive screening.

papers.title: ProRB: a structure-free unified framework for joint prediction and design of protein-RNA interactions.
papers.abstract: While protein-RNA interactions are fundamental to post-transcriptional processes, achieving a holistic understanding of their regulatory logic remains challenging. Current computational models often treat binding affinity, interface mapping, and RNA design as isolated tasks, thereby failing to provide a unified perspective of the protein-RNA interactome. Here, we introduce ProRB, a unified sequence-based framework that jointly estimates protein-RNA binding affinity, predicts binding interfaces in proteins and RNAs, and generates protein-binding RNA sequences from protein sequences. By fusing p
papers.summary: ProRB is a sequence-based computational framework that unifies three tasks related to protein-RNA interactions: predicting binding affinity, mapping binding interfaces on both proteins and RNAs, and designing RNA sequences that bind a given protein. Unlike prior models that treat these tasks separately, ProRB provides a single structure-free model for holistic analysis of the protein-RNA interactome.

papers.title: Characterizing CCR2 homodimers using homology-derived and AI-predicted interfaces.
papers.abstract: Deciphering the functional roles of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) oligomers requires defining their structural organization, which remains a challenge due to the inherent flexibility of their 7 transmembrane (TM) domains. Here, we focused on determining homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2, a major component of the inflammatory response, for which no antagonist has yet been approved. We generated models of CCR2 homodimers combining homology modeling, a conventional in silico approach, or an AI-based AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, with molecular dynamics simulations. We de
papers.summary: This study models the homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2 by combining homology modeling and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions with molecular dynamics simulations. It aims to clarify the structural organization of CCR2 dimers, which is important for understanding its role in inflammation and for future drug development.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides as computational candidates for SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease inhibition.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) remains an attractive antiviral target because of its dual role in viral polyprotein processing and host immune modulation. In this study, we employed an exploratory structure-based computational workflow to identify antimicrobial peptide scaffolds with predicted PLpro-binding potential. A total of 6,615 peptides compiled from public databases were screened using protein-peptide docking, followed by molecular dynamics simulations and end-state binding energy analysis for selected complexes. Among the prioritized candidates, peptides 33,035 and 17,047 sho
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 6,615 antimicrobial peptides from public databases for potential binding to the SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro), an antiviral drug target. Two peptides (33,035 and 17,047) emerged as prioritized candidates with favorable predicted binding properties, suggesting they warrant further experimental validation as potential PLpro inhibitors.

papers.title: DyProL: Dynamic Ensemble Representation Learning for Protein-Nucleic Acid Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions play central roles in gene regulation and cellular function, and extensive efforts have been devoted to predicting nucleic acid binding sites from protein structures. However, protein-nucleic acid recognition is inherently dynamic, whereas most existing computational approaches rely on single static conformations, limiting their ability to capture conformational heterogeneity underlying binding. Here, we present DyProL, an ensemble-based conformational representation learning framework that models proteins as ensembles of conformations sampled from equilibrium
papers.summary: DyProL is a computational framework that predicts protein-nucleic acid binding sites by modeling proteins as ensembles of dynamic conformations rather than single static structures. By learning representations from conformational ensembles sampled from equilibrium, it aims to capture the conformational heterogeneity that underlies binding, addressing a key limitation of prior static-structure approaches.

papers.title: A sustainable functional food ingredient from Saussurea involucrata cell culture alleviates atopic dermatitis-like inflammation via arachidonic acid metabolic remodeling.
papers.abstract: Nutritional interventions may complement established approaches for managing atopic dermatitis (AD). Here, we evaluated Saussurea involucrata cell culture (SIC), a sustainable functional-food material, in a DNCB-induced mouse model of AD-like inflammation. Chemical profiling established the phytochemical composition of SIC, and both topical and oral interventions improved macroscopic and histopathological outcomes. Under the tested conditions, the oral groups showed more consistent changes in systemic indices, providing the basis for subsequent mechanistic analyses. Integrated transcriptomic a
papers.summary: This study evaluates Saussurea involucrata cell culture (SIC), a sustainable functional food ingredient, in a DNCB-induced mouse model of atopic dermatitis. Both topical and oral SIC interventions improved macroscopic and histopathological outcomes, with oral administration showing more consistent systemic changes. Integrated transcriptomic analysis suggests the anti-inflammatory effects are mediated through remodeling of arachidonic acid metabolism.

papers.title: Cooling-induced aggregation in SARA-Modeled crude oils near oil-water interfaces: Molecular mechanisms of interplay among wax, asphaltene, and resin.
papers.abstract: Waxy crude oils under high water cut, low temperature pipeline transport conditions undergo complex gelation upon cooling, yet the interplay between asphaltene, resin, and wax in confined oil layers near oil-water interfaces remain poorly understood. Through molecular dynamics simulations of model crude oil systems with systematically varied SARA compositions, this study reveals the cooperative and competitive mechanisms among these three components. Asphaltene initiates wax crystallization by serving as heterogeneous nucleation sites, whereas resin promotes subsequent crystal growth and enhan
papers.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how wax, asphaltene, and resin interact in model crude oils near oil-water interfaces during cooling. It finds that asphaltene acts as nucleation sites for wax crystallization, while resin promotes crystal growth, revealing cooperative and competitive mechanisms underlying gelation in waxy crude oils.

papers.title: A curated benchmark for cofolding models on kinase conformational states.
papers.abstract: Protein kinases are critical drug targets, requiring therapeutics that can modulate their active and inactive conformational states. While cofolding models can generate global folds directly from kinase sequences and ligand SMILES strings, these models have not yet been tested on their ability to recover ligand-induced-fit conformational states of the kinase proteins. Here, we introduce KinConfBench, a curated benchmark of 2225 high-quality human kinase chains to evaluate the ability of four state-of-the-art cofolding models-Boltz-2, Chai-1, Protenix, and RoseTTAFold-All-Atom-to recover both c
papers.summary: This paper introduces KinConfBench, a curated benchmark of 2,225 high-quality human kinase chains designed to test whether cofolding models can recover ligand-induced conformational states, not just overall folds. The authors evaluate four state-of-the-art cofolding models (Boltz-2, Chai-1, Protenix, and RoseTTAFold-All-Atom) on this task, addressing a gap in how well these tools capture active versus inactive kinase conformations relevant to drug design.

papers.title: Data driven selection of consensus docking pipelines for structure based hit identification.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) is a cornerstone of computer-aided drug design, yet its success depends on selecting a combination of docking tools, scoring function (SF), and ranking strategies. MolDockLab addresses this challenge with an automated, data-driven framework that optimizes SBVS workflows for a protein target, balancing predictive performance and computational efficiency. It systematically explores combinations of five docking engines, 15 SF, and three consensus ranking strategies using a calibration set of ≈ 200 compounds with known bioactivity, and applies the best-corr
papers.summary: MolDockLab is an automated, data-driven framework that optimizes structure-based virtual screening workflows by systematically testing combinations of five docking engines, 15 scoring functions, and three consensus ranking strategies against a calibration set of ~200 compounds with known bioactivity. It selects the best-performing consensus docking pipeline for a given protein target, balancing predictive accuracy with computational cost. This addresses the long-standing challenge of choosing docking tools and scoring functions for hit identification.

papers.title: Mechanistic elucidation of Panax ginseng in improving atherosclerosis via multidimensional artificial intelligence computing coupled with experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is the core pathological foundation of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, and its efficient prevention is pivotal to lowering related mortality and disability. Panax ginseng confers remarkable cardiovascular protection, whereas its anti-atherosclerotic efficacy and intrinsic mechanisms remain poorly elucidated, restricting its clinical translation. This study sought to decipher the mechanism underlying Panax ginseng mediated AS improvement via multidimensional artificial intelligence (AI) computation integrated with experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study combines multidimensional AI computational approaches with experimental validation to uncover how Panax ginseng improves atherosclerosis. The authors identify mechanistic pathways underlying ginseng's cardiovascular protective effects, aiming to support its clinical translation for atherosclerosis prevention.

papers.title: Novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus: Distribution in reproductive organs and integrated biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: While the chemical constituents of flower buds from several Panax species have been reported, the phytochemical profile of the flower buds of Vietnamese ginseng remains understudied, particularly alkaloids. This study aimed to characterize alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus (PVF), investigate their distribution across reproductive plant parts, and their biological relevance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus, a previously understudied Vietnamese ginseng variety. The authors map the distribution of these alkaloids across reproductive organs and evaluate their biological activities, expanding the known phytochemical profile of Panax species.

papers.title: Coix Seed Attenuates Acute Lung Injury via NLRP3 Signaling Pathway: Efficacy, Active Components, and Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Coix seed is a medicinal and nutritional resource, but its protective effects against acute lung injury (ALI) remain unclear. This study investigated the efficacy, active components, and mechanisms of Coix seed extract (CSE) against ALI, focusing on the NLRP3 signaling pathway. The therapeutic efficacy of CSE was evaluated in a murine model of ALI. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry identified 32 components in CSE, which were then analyzed via network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations for target prediction and drug-likeness evaluation. In vivo effects on
papers.summary: This study shows that Coix seed extract reduces acute lung injury in mice, with effects linked to the NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathway. Using LC-MS, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations, the authors identified 32 components and predicted their targets, suggesting multiple active compounds contribute to the protective effect.

papers.title: SMILES2Docking: An Open-Source Desktop Workflow for Ligand Ionization, Stereochemistry-Aware Preparation and Semi-Empirical 3D Refinement.
papers.abstract: SMILES2Docking converts spreadsheet-based SMILES libraries into docking-ready 3D ligands through a single, configurable pipeline. Salt and coformer removal, a three-mode stereocenter policy, prediction of the dominant protonation state with a graph neural network pKa model (MolGpKa) refined by iterative titration, distance-geometry embedding with RDKit, a molecular-mechanics optimization cascade, and an optional semi-empirical refinement under an implicit solvation model are combined in one tool, with records processed either sequentially or distributed across CPU cores. Users select among per
papers.summary: SMILES2Docking is an open-source desktop workflow that converts spreadsheet-based SMILES libraries into docking-ready 3D ligands through a single configurable pipeline. It combines salt/coformer removal, stereocenter handling, GNN-based pKa prediction (MolGpKa) with iterative titration, RDKit distance-geometry embedding, MM optimization, and optional semi-empirical refinement with implicit solvation, supporting parallel processing across CPU cores.

papers.title: From wireframes to immersive reality: a historical perspective on molecular visualization software.
papers.abstract: The evolution of molecular visualization software represents a pivotal yet often underappreciated dimension of computational structural biology and bioinformatics. As the scale and complexity of structural datasets increase, spanning from cryo-electron microscopy reconstructions to proteome-wide AI-predicted models, visualization tools have become essential for data interpretation, hypothesis generation, and effective scientific communication. Widely used platforms such as PyMOL, UCSF Chimera, and emerging virtual reality environments reflect decades of progressive innovation driven by advance
papers.summary: This review traces the historical evolution of molecular visualization software, from early wireframe representations to modern immersive virtual reality environments. It highlights how tools like PyMOL and UCSF Chimera have become essential for interpreting increasingly complex structural data, including cryo-EM reconstructions and AI-predicted proteome-wide models. The paper argues that visualization is a pivotal but underappreciated dimension of computational structural biology.

papers.title: Recent Exploration of Right-Handed D-Sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as Potential Tools Toward α-Helical Mimicry.
papers.abstract: Over the last 15 years, our laboratory has explored peptidomimetics in diverse research areas, including AApeptide folding, structure-based design, combinatorial screening, and supramolecular chemistry. Through these efforts, we successfully introduced a new subclass of AApeptides known as sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides. In recent years, we took advantage of the synthetic scaffold and rationally designed and developed helices targeting a series of protein-protein interactions. This Perspective summarizes our recent advances in developing right-handed helical D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, which closely resem
papers.summary: This perspective reviews the authors' work developing right-handed helical D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, a class of peptidomimetics designed to mimic α-helices. These synthetic scaffolds can be rationally designed to target specific protein-protein interactions, offering potential as therapeutic tools.

papers.title: Standardizing pre-existing anti-PEG antibody detection: A key to clarifying their binding features and clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) is a widely used pharmaceutical excipient to improve drug solubility and prolong in vivo circulation duration. Although it was initially considered non-immunogenic, recent studies have confirmed the ubiquitous presence of anti-PEG antibodies pre-existing in human, influencing the efficacy and safety of multiple PEGylated medicines. Due to the contradictions of current anti-PEG antibody detection methods and unclear induction mechanism of human pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies, the actual prevalence, binding features, and biological effects of pre-existing anti-PEG ant
papers.summary: This paper addresses the lack of standardized methods for detecting pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies in humans, which are common and can affect the safety and efficacy of PEGylated drugs. It argues that inconsistent detection approaches have led to contradictory prevalence estimates and unclear binding characteristics, and calls for standardization to clarify their clinical relevance.

papers.title: The ER-Golgi Lipid Exchanger PsORP1 Is Essential for Phytophthora sojae Development and Is Blocked by Oxathiapiprolin via Its OSBP-Related Domain (ORD).
papers.abstract: Oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP)-related proteins (ORPs) are indispensable eukaryotic lipid transporters and promising targets for pharmaceutical and agrochemical exploitation. Among ORP family members across kingdoms, oomycete ORP1 constitutes a phylogenetically distinct subtype that evolved independently in oomycetes, which is markedly divergent from ORP homologues in animals, plants and fungi. Oxathiapiprolin, the first commercial fungicide targeting OSBP family proteins, specifically acts on oomycete ORP1 and exhibits robust inhibitory efficacy against diverse Phytophthora pathogens and do
papers.summary: This study shows that the oomycete-specific lipid exchanger PsORP1 is essential for the development of the plant pathogen Phytophthora sojae, functioning at the ER-Golgi interface. The fungicide oxathiapiprolin blocks this protein by binding its OSBP-related domain (ORD), explaining its potent anti-Phytophthora activity. The work highlights oomycete ORP1 as a distinct and valuable target for crop protection.

papers.title: Molecular recognition of VEGF165 by DNA aptamers: insights from an integrated computational framework.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor 165 (VEGF165) is a homodimeric angiogenic protein composed of a receptor-binding domain (RBD) and a heparin-binding domain (HBD) connected by a flexible linker. The absence of a complete experimental structure of full-length VEGF165 has limited atomic-level understanding of its recognition by DNA aptamers. In this work, we reconstructed the full-length VEGF165 structure. Accelerated molecular dynamics simulations were employed to generate a representative conformational ensemble for ensemble docking, followed by molecular dynamics simulations and MM/GBSA calc
papers.summary: This study reconstructs the full-length structure of VEGF165, a key angiogenic protein lacking complete experimental structural data, and uses accelerated molecular dynamics, ensemble docking, and MM/GBSA calculations to investigate how DNA aptamers recognize it. The integrated computational framework provides atomic-level insights into aptamer binding to VEGF165, which could inform the design of improved therapeutic aptamers.

papers.title: Near-Infrared Fluorescent PROTAC Enables Theranostic Imaging and Selective Tau Degradation in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: The hyperphosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) protein plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by driving neurofibrillary tangle formation and neuronal dysfunction. While proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) offer a promising approach for directly eliminating pathogenic proteins, their real-time visualization in living systems remains challenging. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of a series of near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent Tau-targeting degraders that integrate theranostic imaging with targeted protein degradation. Among them, compound D9 emerges as a
papers.summary: This paper reports the design of near-infrared fluorescent PROTAC molecules that both visualize and degrade hyperphosphorylated Tau, a key driver of Alzheimer's disease pathology. The lead compound D9 enables real-time imaging of Tau in living systems while selectively promoting its degradation, offering a combined theranostic strategy for AD.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure-based discovery of etravirine as a specific inhibitor of PRMT5/pICln protein-protein interaction for prostate cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) is overexpressed in many cancers and correlates with poor patient survival. In prostate cancer, PRMT5 cooperates with its cofactor pICln to promote tumour growth by epigenetically activating androgen receptor (AR) expression. Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, we identified a previously undefined, pICln-specific protein-protein interaction (PPI) interface on PRMT5, termed P4I. Structure-based virtual screening identified the FDA-approved compound etravirine as a binder to this site. BiFC, Co-IP, and PLA assays confir
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of the PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, the authors identified a previously undefined pICln-specific protein-protein interaction interface on PRMT5, termed P4I. Structure-based virtual screening of this site identified the FDA-approved drug etravirine as a specific inhibitor of the PRMT5/pICln interaction, with potential for treating prostate cancer by disrupting epigenetic activation of the androgen receptor.

papers.title: Rational and computation-assisted engineering of a compact and efficient CRISPR-Cas12f genome editor.
papers.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas12f system is an ultracompact genome-editing platform, yet only a few orthologs exhibit robust activity in mammalian cells. Here, we systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, capable of genome editing in human cells. sgRNA scaffold optimization enhanced the basal activity of PspCas12f1. To further improve its performance, we combined structure-guided rational design with protein language model-assisted filtering. Candidate mutations predicted by SaProt were further screened based on structural proximity to the DNA-b
papers.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
papers.summary: The study systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, that enable genome editing in human cells. By optimizing the sgRNA scaffold and combining structure-guided rational design with a protein language model (SaProt) to filter mutations near the DNA-binding interface, the authors engineered a compact and highly efficient CRISPR-Cas12f editor. This work expands the toolbox of small Cas enzymes suitable for viral delivery in gene therapy.

papers.title: A computational framework integrating a protein language model with alchemical simulation for gain-of-function enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Engineering enzymes with enhanced activity and stability is a central goal of biotechnology, yet the inherent trade-off between optimizing global protein fitness and specific substrate binding affinity poses a significant challenge. Here, we present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that synergistically integrates a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to overcome this limitation. Our workflow employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuned ESM-2 model to perform high-throughput saturation mutagenesis, rapidly identifying mutations that preserve protein fi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that combines a fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation simulations to design gain-of-function enzymes. The language model rapidly screens saturation mutagenesis libraries for mutations that preserve protein fitness, while FEP then evaluates substrate binding affinity, addressing the trade-off between global stability and specific activity. This hybrid approach aims to make enzyme engineering more efficient and accurate.

papers.title: Design of peptides with non-canonical amino acids using flow matching.
papers.abstract: The canonical vocabulary of twenty amino acids limits the chemical space available to proteins and peptides. Expanding this vocabulary to hundreds of non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) allows the engineering of proteins with novel function and activity, and is of particular interest for therapeutic peptides such as macrocycles, where ncAAs can improve proteolytic stability, membrane permeability and immunogenicity. However, existing structure-based design tools either cannot model ncAAs at all, or are restricted to a small, fixed vocabulary of ncAAs seen during training, and ncAA data in the Pr
papers.summary: This paper introduces a flow-matching generative model for designing peptides that incorporate non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs), overcoming the limitation of existing tools that either ignore ncAAs or only handle a small fixed set seen during training. The approach expands the chemical design space for therapeutic peptides like macrocycles, where ncAAs can improve stability, permeability, and immunogenicity.

papers.title: Methionine γ-lyase traps cofactor pyridoxal-5'-phosphate through specific serine-mediated affinity.
papers.abstract: Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP), the ubiquitous and ancient cofactor, plays important roles in enzymatic elimination, transamination and other reactions. The catalytic efficiency of PLP-dependent enzymes is significantly higher than that of free PLP. The recruitment of solution PLP by the enzymes, particularly through interactions outside the active-site entrance, is the key step determining the occurrence of PLP-mediated catalysis. However, the precise mechanism by which enzymes recruit solution PLP remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates how methionine γ-lyase captures the cofactor pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP) from solution, revealing that a specific serine residue mediates high-affinity binding that traps PLP within the enzyme. The work provides structural and mechanistic insight into cofactor recruitment, a key step for PLP-dependent catalysis that was previously poorly understood.

papers.title: Orbital Tuning of the β-Lactam Warhead: Intrinsic n → π* Preactivation in Cephalosporins.
papers.abstract: The stability-reactivity paradox of β-lactam antibiotics remains a fundamental puzzle in medicinal chemistry: how can cephalosporins maintain high antibacterial efficacy despite having reduced ring strain compared to penicillins? Here, we reveal the intrinsic conformational architecture of 7-aminodesacetoxycephalosporanic acid (7-ADCA), the foundational core of cephalosporins, using laser ablation broadband rotational spectroscopy and high-level quantum chemical calculations. In a striking departure from the hydrogen-bond-mediated activation observed in penicillins, we discovered that 7-ADCA c
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: This study uses rotational spectroscopy and quantum chemistry to show that the cephalosporin core (7-ADCA) achieves β-lactam reactivity through an intrinsic orbital interaction (n → π* preactivation) rather than the hydrogen-bond-mediated activation seen in penicillins. This resolves the long-standing paradox of how cephalosporins remain potent despite lower ring strain.

papers.title: Lipid Nanoparticle Protein Coronas Arise through Lipoprotein Fusion Rather Than Shell-like Adsorption.
papers.abstract: The protein corona influences the in vivo biodistribution of ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) in nucleic acid delivery, yet their structural architecture remains poorly defined. Using cryo-transmission electron microscopy, we visualized LNP-protein interactions in their native state. We show that, unlike the discrete "fuzzy" shells observed on hard nanoparticles, LNPs displayed no peripheral protein shell. Instead, controlled incubation and competitive "dual-particle" assays, supported by molecular dynamics simulations, indicate that LNP membranes undergo localized thickening and electron-
papers.summary: Using cryo-electron microscopy, the authors show that ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) used for nucleic acid delivery do not acquire a conventional shell-like protein corona. Instead, proteins associate with LNPs through lipoprotein fusion, causing localized membrane thickening rather than peripheral adsorption. This structural insight could reshape how LNP biodistribution and targeting are understood and engineered.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme pH Optima from Structure Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Enzyme activity and stability are strongly modulated by pH, making the catalytic pH optimum (pHopt) a key parameter in enzyme development and biotechnological applications. Experimental determination of pHopt is, however, labor-intensive and time-consuming, motivating the development of accurate computational prediction methods. Here, we introduce pHoptNN, an E(n)-equivariant graph neural network designed to predict enzyme pHopt directly from three-dimensional protein structures. pHoptNN was trained on a curated data set comprising nearly 12,000 enzymes with experimentally determined pHopt val
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present pHoptNN, an E(n)-equivariant graph neural network that predicts an enzyme's optimal catalytic pH directly from its 3D protein structure. Trained on nearly 12,000 enzymes with experimentally measured pH optima, the model offers a fast computational alternative to labor-intensive experimental pHopt determination. This could accelerate enzyme engineering and biotechnological applications where pH behavior is critical.

papers.title: [Effects of astragaloside Ⅰ on full-thickness skin defects in diabetic rats and its underlying mechanism].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the effects of astragaloside Ⅰ (AS-Ⅰ) on full-thickness skin defects in diabetic rats and its underlying mechanism. Methods: This study was an experimental study with grouped design and repeated measures design. Twenty-four male Sprague-Dawley rats aged 6-8 weeks were divided into control group (n=6) and modeling group (n=18) using a random number table method (the same grouping method was used throughout). After successful induction of diabetes mellitus, the modeling group was further divided into model group, low-dose AS-Ⅰ group, and high-dose AS-Ⅰ group, with 6 rat
papers.journal: Zhonghua shao shang yu chuang mian xiu fu za zhi
papers.summary: This study investigated whether astragaloside I (AS-I), a compound derived from the traditional Chinese herb Astragalus, can promote healing of full-thickness skin wounds in diabetic rats. Diabetic rats with skin defects were treated with low or high doses of AS-I, and healing outcomes and underlying molecular mechanisms were assessed. The findings suggest AS-I may accelerate wound healing in diabetes, potentially offering a therapeutic approach for diabetic wound complications.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a multi-epitope subunit vaccine against Salmonella Enteritidis infection.
papers.abstract: Salmonella Enteritidis (S. Enteritidis) is a major pathogen causing foodborne diseases worldwide, posing a serious threat to public health security and the sustainable development of the poultry industry. To overcome the limitations of conventional vaccines in terms of efficacy, safety, and cross-protection, a novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine (SEMV) was designed and constructed using an immunoinformatics-based strategy. Through systematic screening of epitopes from key immunogenic proteins of S. Enteritidis (SseB, SipC, OmpD and TolC), a total of 8 B-cell epitopes, 4 MHC-I-restricted epitop
papers.summary: This study designed a multi-epitope subunit vaccine (SEMV) against Salmonella Enteritidis using immunoinformatics, selecting B-cell and MHC-I epitopes from four immunogenic proteins (SseB, SipC, OmpD, TolC). The vaccine was constructed and evaluated, aiming to overcome efficacy, safety, and cross-protection limitations of conventional vaccines. It represents a computational design approach with potential for poultry vaccine development.

papers.title: Unveiling the molecular toxicity of plasticizers derived from microplastics (DMP and DEP) in diabetic kidney disease: integrative insights from network toxicology and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a prevalent microvascular complication with limited therapeutic options. This study aimed to identify biomarkers associated with microplastic-associated plasticizers in DKD and to explore their potential molecular mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology with multi-omics data to investigate how microplastic-derived plasticizers (DMP and DEP) may contribute to diabetic kidney disease. The authors identify candidate biomarkers and propose molecular mechanisms linking plasticizer exposure to DKD pathology.

papers.title: Multiscale mechanistic modeling for the rational design of novel dual-target candidates against acetylcholinesterase and NADPH oxidase: an advanced computational study.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative illness strongly associated with oxidative stress, which requires immediate intervention for therapeutic agents with potent antioxidant properties.
papers.summary: This study uses multiscale computational modeling to rationally design dual-target drug candidates that simultaneously inhibit acetylcholinesterase and NADPH oxidase, two proteins implicated in Alzheimer's disease pathology and oxidative stress. The work demonstrates how integrated mechanistic simulations can guide the discovery of multi-target therapeutics rather than relying on single-target approaches.

papers.title: Repurposing MK0873 as a non-covalent hTERT-Targeting compound: a proof of concept study.
papers.abstract: Telomerase is a key regulator of both cellular immortality and aging, making it an attractive target for cancer therapy and age associated pathologies. Its clinical exploitation has been limited by structural complexity and challenges in achieving specificity. Recent structural insights into human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) have enabled the identification of selective inhibitors. Here, we repurposed MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously evaluated in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis and COPD, as a non covalent telomerase targeting agent. In silico docking and molecu
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study repurposes MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor already tested in Phase II clinical trials, as a non-covalent inhibitor of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) using in silico docking and molecular approaches. The work suggests an existing clinical-stage drug could be redirected toward telomerase-targeting cancer and aging therapies, potentially accelerating translational development.

papers.title: Targeting IDH-driven Oncometabolism in glioblastoma: a computational approach for the identification of potential inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor frequently driven by mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1 and IDH2) enzymes, which promote neomorphic synthesis of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) and subsequent metabolic dysfunction. Although these mutations are associated with different clinical outcomes, therapeutic intervention remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, restricted blood-brain barrier permeability, drug efflux mechanisms, and effective DNA repair pathways. Therefore, this study aims to identify selective inhibitors of mutant IDH pro
papers.summary: This study uses computational drug discovery methods to identify potential selective inhibitors of mutant IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes, which drive glioblastoma through production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate. The work targets a well-known cancer metabolic vulnerability, though the abstract is truncated and the specific compounds or validation results are not fully described.

papers.title: Elucidating adverse drug reactions and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin through pharmacovigilance and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: The comprehensive safety profile and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin-associated adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remain to be fully elucidated.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study combines pharmacovigilance data with multi-omics analysis to characterize adverse drug reactions associated with ivermectin and explore their underlying molecular mechanisms. It aims to provide a more comprehensive safety profile for the drug by linking clinical ADR signals to biological pathways.

papers.title: Deep DNA and protein level feature integration for robust clinical variant interpretation using probabilistic gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: A major challenge in clinical genomics is to classify genetic variations correctly, since it directly affects disease diagnosis and personal care. The existing methods tend to be based on the combination of different factors, such as protein structure, population frequencies, phenotypic annotations, and sequence conservation. Nevertheless, these methods often cannot be used to achieve the necessary interpretability, quantify uncertainty, and address rare cases. This paper presents a probabilistic gradient boosting model on variant pathogenicity prediction. The suggested framework applies biolo
papers.summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic gradient boosting model that integrates DNA-level and protein-level features to improve clinical variant pathogenicity prediction. The framework aims to provide better interpretability and uncertainty quantification than existing multi-factor methods, particularly for rare variants.

papers.title: Anti-Lung Cancer Agent Discovery and Development: A Review of Cross-Platform Correlation Across in silico, Network Pharmacology, in vitro, and in vivo Assessments.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for more effective and clinically translatable therapeutic agents. In recent years, drug discovery strategies integrating computational modeling with experimental validation have gained increasing attention; however, their predictive consistency across biological scales remains a critical challenge. This review systematically synthesises evidence from eleven primary studies that evaluated anti-lung cancer agents across computational, cellular, and organism-level platforms within a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from eleven primary studies that evaluated anti-lung cancer agents using integrated computational, network pharmacology, in vitro, and in vivo approaches. It highlights the challenge of maintaining predictive consistency across biological scales and assesses how well in silico predictions translate to experimental validation. The work provides guidance on cross-platform correlation for more reliable anti-lung cancer drug discovery.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using an integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics approach. By combining toxicological prediction tools with multi-omics data, the authors aim to identify molecular mechanisms and pathways linking PFOA exposure to MASLD pathogenesis from a systems biology perspective.

papers.title: Repurposing of lansoprazole and nitazoxanide as NR2F2 inhibitors in the gastric cancer cell line GCIY: computational insights and siRNA-mediated in vitro tests.
papers.abstract: Nuclear receptors (NRs) are a superfamily of ligand-activated transcription factors that mediate the cellular response to hormones, vitamins, and dietary lipids, thus orchestrating numerous physiological processes and influencing multiple disease states. Within this superfamily, NR2Fs, also known as Chicken Ovalbumin Upstream Promoter Transcription Factor (COUP-TF), are a family of nuclear orphan receptors, due to the lack of known endogenous ligands. Among them, NR2F2 transcription factor activities involve regulation of cell differentiation during organogenesis, maintenance of adult tissue h
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to identify lansoprazole and nitazoxanide as potential inhibitors of the orphan nuclear receptor NR2F2, a transcription factor implicated in gastric cancer. The authors then validate these predictions in the GCIY gastric cancer cell line using siRNA-mediated knockdown, showing that NR2F2 inhibition affects cancer cell behavior. The work suggests a drug repurposing strategy for targeting NR2F2 in gastric cancer.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study uses computational and experimental methods to show that naringenin, a natural flavonoid, can simultaneously inhibit RAGE-NF-κB inflammatory signaling and interfere with Aβ fibrillization, suggesting a dual-target strategy for Alzheimer's disease. The integrated approach identifies naringenin as a potential therapeutic candidate that may overcome limitations of single-target drugs.

papers.title: Screening and characterization of pro-angiogenic peptides from Spirulina: computer simulation, experimental validation, and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: In this study, we identified novel pro-angiogenic peptides from Spirulina and elucidated their molecular mechanisms. Among the three fractions (A, B, and C) purified from the Spirulina protein extract by RP-HPLC, fraction B displayed the most potent pro-angiogenic activity. Through LC-MS/MS analysis, bioinformatics screening, and molecular docking, 20 candidate peptides were selected. In zebrafish models, five of these peptides, MFDCLR, MDMWGK, MNPGCR, MYDNFCK, and MPGLGR, significantly stimulated subintestinal vessel plexus (SIVP) growth and rescued intersegmental vessel (ISV) injury induced
papers.summary: This study identified five novel pro-angiogenic peptides (MFDCLR, MDMWGK, MNPGCR, MYDNFCK, MPGLGR) from Spirulina using a combination of LC-MS/MS, bioinformatics screening, and molecular docking, followed by validation in zebrafish models. The peptides significantly promoted subintestinal vessel plexus growth and rescued intersegmental vessel injury, with mechanistic insights into their angiogenic activity.

papers.title: Comparative and Subtractive Genomics Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains for Novel Target Identification and Drug Repurposing Strategies.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae has created a major global health challenge due to the limited availability of conserved therapeutic targets effective across diverse resistant strains. In this study, an integrative computational target-discovery and drug-repurposing framework was applied to six clinically relevant K. pneumoniae strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 3012 conserved genes, which were subsequently filtered to nine essential, non-host homologous proteins. Among these, three conserved cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prior
papers.summary: This study used comparative and subtractive genomics to identify conserved drug targets across six multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, narrowing 3012 conserved genes down to nine essential, non-host-homologous proteins. Three cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prioritized as promising targets, and drug repurposing strategies were explored against them. The work provides a computational framework for finding new therapeutic options against antibiotic-resistant infections.

papers.title: Sesamum indicum-derived valdiate as a novel neuroprotective agent targeting PDE10A2 and SIRT1 in Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease is prevalent globally, with approximately 4.88 cases per 100,000 people, based on a systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies published between 2010 and 2022. Despite its significant prevalence, no proper treatment is available that directly addresses Huntington's disease. The existing treatments focus on symptom management, such as controlling chorea and psychiatric symptoms. The drugs used for this purpose may also cause side effects, including depression and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies a compound derived from Sesamum indicum (sesame) that may act as a neuroprotective agent in Huntington's disease by targeting the proteins PDE10A2 and SIRT1. Using bioinformatics approaches, the authors propose this natural compound as a potential therapeutic candidate, though the abstract primarily emphasizes the lack of effective treatments and the global prevalence of the disease.

papers.title: Large language models in bioinformatics: a comprehensive survey.
papers.abstract: The emergence of foundation models with trillion-level parameters has redefined the landscape of artificial intelligence. Various fields are developing their own large-scale models, which can solve many problems within the field and improve work efficiency. Biological large-scale models are a cross-disciplinary research field that combines mathematics, computer science, and biology, aiming to simulate and understand the structure, function, and dynamic changes of biological systems through the establishment of complex computational models. This field covers multiple levels such as biological p
papers.summary: This survey reviews the application of large language models (LLMs) and foundation models in bioinformatics, covering how these trillion-parameter models are being adapted to biological problems across multiple scales. It provides a cross-disciplinary overview of how computational models can simulate and understand biological structure, function, and dynamics.

papers.title: A voyage of reprogrammable metabolic bioengineering reshapes plant defense: from editing tools to synthetic systems.
papers.abstract: Metabolic bioengineering has emerged as a transformative approach for reshaping plant defense by targeting intrinsic biosynthetic pathways to enhance immunity in modern agriculture. Moving beyond proof-of-concept metabolomics to broad-spectrum programmable pathway engineering addresses gaps in plant rational design and optimizes resilience in response to diverse environmental cues. This review aims to comprehensively highlight the transition of innovative approaches to phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids, inferring adaptive reprogramming that mediates the growth-de
papers.summary: This review surveys how metabolic bioengineering can be used to reprogram plant biosynthetic pathways—covering phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids—to strengthen plant immunity. It traces the field's shift from proof-of-concept metabolomics toward programmable, broad-spectrum pathway engineering for more resilient crops.

papers.title: PLK1/FOXM1-associated tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) have been widely studied in various cancers; however, their expression characteristics in endometrial cancer (EC) and their potential association with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the expression of PLK1 and FOXM1 in endometrial cancer and links them to a specific tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in the tumor microenvironment. The findings suggest that PLK1/FOXM1 activity may shape immune remodeling in endometrial cancer, potentially informing prognosis or therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Nanogel-Based Precision Bone Regeneration: Rational Design, Biological Barrier Penetration, and Osteoporotic Microenvironment Remodeling.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of osteoporosis is primarily associated with impaired communication between osteoblasts and osteoclasts, leading to disrupted bone homeostasis. Conventional biomaterials mainly rely on macroscopic structural support and are limited in their ability to precisely regulate the complex bone microenvironment and overcome biological barriers. As representative soft matter nanoplatforms, nanogels possess unique viscoelastic mechanical properties and adaptive biointerfacial properties, offering new opportunities to overcome physical barriers within bone tissues. Moving beyond previous
papers.summary: This review discusses nanogel-based platforms for bone regeneration, focusing on their rational design, ability to penetrate biological barriers, and capacity to remodel the osteoporotic microenvironment by targeting the impaired communication between osteoblasts and osteoclasts. It argues that nanogels' viscoelastic and adaptive biointerfacial properties offer advantages over conventional macroscopic biomaterials for precise bone microenvironment regulation.

papers.title: Orphan GPCRs in diabetes mellitus: metabolic control, inflammation, and drug development.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (diabetes) is a major health burden with the highest mortality rate, affecting an estimated 537 million adults worldwide. The treatment of diabetes remains complex owing to insulin resistance, β-cell dysfunction, metabolic inflammation, and progressive organ damage. While G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) selectively suppress many pathological diseases, the functional characteristics of orphan GPCRs (oGPCRs) remain unexplored as therapeutic targets for diabetes. This review comprehensively evaluates oGPCRs and their roles in diabetes. Orphan receptors are classified based o
papers.summary: This review examines orphan G-protein-coupled receptors (oGPCRs) as potential therapeutic targets for diabetes, focusing on their roles in metabolic control, inflammation, and disease progression. It highlights how these understudied receptors could offer new avenues for drug development given the limitations of current diabetes treatments.

papers.title: Functional and mechanistic characterization of the phosphatidyl-myo-inositol mannosyltransferase PimA from Mycobacterium tuberculosis: implications for anti-tuberculosis drug development.
papers.abstract: Human-adapted Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) also infects animals and transmits zoonotically, threatening public health. The cell wall glycolipids lipoarabinomannan and lipomannan are essential virulence factors of Mtb. Phosphatidyl-myo-inositol mannosyltransferase PimA catalyzes a key step in their biosynthesis and represents a potential drug target. However, the functional mechanism of Mtb PimA remains incompletely understood. Here, the hydrodynamic diameter of monomeric PimA was measured as 5.1 ± 0.2 nm. The structural model of PimA was predicted using AlphaFold2. Molecular docking was co
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study characterizes PimA, a key enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall glycolipid biosynthesis, using biophysical measurements and AlphaFold2-based structural modeling. The authors provide mechanistic insights into PimA's function that could inform the design of anti-tuberculosis drugs targeting this enzyme.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Natural-Product Aromatase (CYP19A1) Inhibitors via Integrated Molecular Docking and QSAR Modelling.
papers.abstract: Aromatase (CYP19A1) is the rate-limiting enzyme in estrogen biosynthesis and the principal therapeutic target for estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Despite the clinical success of third-generation aromatase inhibitors (AIs) such as letrozole and anastrozole, acquired resistance and systemic adverse effects, including musculoskeletal pain, bone density loss, and cardiovascular complications, which necessitate the identification of novel scaffolds. This study employs an integrated computational pipeline combining ligand-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) mode
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling and molecular docking to screen natural products for their ability to inhibit aromatase (CYP19A1), a key enzyme in estrogen production and a target for ER+ breast cancer therapy. The goal is to identify novel natural-product scaffolds that could overcome resistance and side effects associated with current aromatase inhibitors like letrozole and anastrozole.

papers.title: De Novo Molecular Design and Bioactivity Prediction of Novel Hexahydroquinolines as Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (CDPK4) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (PfCDPK4) is a validated target for malaria transmission-blocking interventions, as its inhibition disrupts male gametocyte exflagellation. Hexahydroquinolines (HHQs) have emerged as promising gametocytocidal agents. This study aimed to design novel HHQs as potential PfCDPK4 inhibitors with good binding affinity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and structural stability. A library of 20,000 novel HHQ analogs was generated using genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design in AlvaBuilder and systematically filtered through a pipeline com
papers.summary: This study used genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design to generate a library of 20,000 novel hexahydroquinoline analogs targeting the malaria transmission-blocking protein PfCDPK4. The compounds were filtered for binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and structural stability, identifying promising candidates as potential antimalarial agents.

papers.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
papers.summary: This study uses chemoinformatics and molecular docking to identify galangin derivatives as potential inhibitors of the HTLV-1 protease, a key enzyme in T-cell leukemia virus type 1. The authors screen natural flavonoid derivatives and predict several candidates with favorable binding affinity and drug-like properties, proposing them as leads for antiviral development. The work is entirely computational, so experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: p70S6K as a Potential Anti-COVID-19 Target: Insights from Wet Bench and In Silico Studies
papers.abstract: The onset of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2019 sparked a global COVID-19 pandemic. This infection is marked by a significant rise in both viral and host kinase activity. Our primary objective was to identify a pivotal host kinase essential for COVID-19 infection and the associated phenomenon of the cytokine storm, which may lead to long-term COVID-19 complications irrespective of viral genetic variations. To achieve this, our study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages following SPIKE transfection over time. Among the kinases surveyed, p70S6K (RPS6KB1) exhibited a 3.5-fold
papers.summary: This study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages after SPIKE transfection and identified p70S6K (RPS6KB1) as a host kinase showing a 3.5-fold increase, suggesting it plays a pivotal role in COVID-19 infection and the associated cytokine storm. The authors propose p70S6K as a potential anti-COVID-19 therapeutic target based on combined wet bench and in silico evidence.
